title: No-bake chocolate cheesecake
subtitle: a rich, firm chocolate cheesecake set with cream, no oven required
excerpt: This chocolate cheesecake uses melted dark chocolate and whipped cream to set the filling without the oven. The texture is dense and moussey, and the biscuit base provides the crunch. It needs at least four hours in the fridge to set properly, so make it the day before. It will keep refrigerated for three days.
sourceNotes: No-bake chocolate cheesecake is a standard British home-baking recipe widely published from the 1980s onward. Method from standard contemporary British home-baking practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cheesecake that firms up through chilling rather than baking. The texture relies on fat content from the cream cheese and whipped cream rather than egg proteins.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the set cheesecake (without any topping) in its tin. Defrost overnight in the fridge. The texture is slightly denser after freezing.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead; keep refrigerated. Add any topping just before serving.

content.text: held together by the fat from cream cheese and whipped double cream, with melted dark chocolate for flavour and additional structure. Use full-fat cream cheese: low-fat versions contain more water and the filling may not set firmly.

Crush the digestive biscuits to fine crumbs (in a food processor or in a bag with a rolling pin). Mix with the melted butter until evenly combined. Press firmly into the base of a lightly greased 23 cm springform tin. Refrigerate while you make the filling.
Melt the dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water, stirring until smooth. Remove from the heat and leave to cool to room temperature (about 15 minutes).
Beat the cream cheese and icing sugar together in a large bowl until smooth. Add the vanilla extract and the cooled melted chocolate, and beat until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, whip the cold double cream to soft peaks. Fold the whipped cream gently into the chocolate cream cheese mixture in three additions, keeping as much air as possible.
Spoon the filling onto the biscuit base and smooth the surface with a palette knife. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until set firmly.

Run a warm palette knife around the inside edge of the tin before releasing the springform clip. Transfer to a serving plate and add any topping (shaved chocolate, fresh berries, or a dusting of cocoa) immediately before serving.

attrs.problem: Filling is soft and does not hold its shape when sliced
attrs.avoid: Avoid using low-fat cream cheese or under-whipped cream.
attrs.fix: If the cheesecake is not set after 4 hours, leave overnight. If still soft, the cream was likely under-whipped or the chocolate was added before it was cool enough.

attrs.problem: Filling has lumps of cream cheese
attrs.avoid: Avoid using cold cream cheese straight from the fridge; it will not beat smooth.
attrs.fix: Take the cream cheese out an hour before mixing so it reaches room temperature.
